people.name: Eileen McMahon
bio: Eileen McMahon is a Nurse Practitioner and Clinical Educational Lead at Hannam Fertility Centre in Toronto with extensive clinical, academic, and leadership experience in reproductive health.

She earned a BA in Nursing Science, a Master's degree in Nursing, along with a post-Master's Nurse Practitioner Diploma and is an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Toronto, where she is actively involved in education and mentorship.

Eileen served on the Board of Directors of the Canadian Fertility and Andrology Society from 2016 to 2021. She made history as CFAS's first nurse President and remains actively involved as an Executive Member of the Nursing Special Interest Group.

people.name: Sari Shaicovitch
bio: Registered Social Worker with more than 25 years of clinical experience, focused on infertility, reproductive loss, anxiety and depression.

people.name: Dr. Rebecca Greenberg
bio: Dr. Rebecca Greenberg is a nurse and bioethicist with two decades of experience in healthcare. She has spent most of her career working in academic hospitals including The Hospital for Sick Children and Sinai Health, and is an Adjunct Professor at the University of Toronto.

She is committed to helping individuals and organizations navigate ethically difficult decisions. She developed and directed the Fellowship in Neonatal-Perinatal Ethics with the Toronto Centre for Neonatal Health and the University of Toronto — the first of its kind in Canada.
Dr. Greenberg is committed to education and sharing her research through speaking internationally, publishing research papers, editing books, and being featured in the media.

people.name: Dr. Ariel Dalfen
bio: Dr. Ariel Dalfen is CEO and Co-Founder of BRIA, and a psychiatrist with over 25 years of experience in women's mental health across all reproductive stages. She previously led Ontario's largest hospital-based perinatal mental health program and authored 'When Baby Brings the Blues'.

people.name: Dr. Bev Young
bio: Dr. Bev Young is CMO and Co-Founder of BRIA, and a psychiatrist with over 25 years of experience in women's mental health, specializing in perinatal, perimenopause, and reproductive psychiatric care.

people.name: Michelle Amato
bio: Registered Nurse, lactation consultant, and BRIA Care Coordinator Manager with more than 25 years in women's healthcare. She specializes in Behavioural Activation (BA) therapy across reproductive life stages.

people.name: Nicole Schroeder
bio: Registered Social Worker with post-graduate training in Emotion Focused Therapy and sex therapy, focused on sexual health in perimenopause.

people.name: Lauren Rose
bio: Registered Dietitian with over 30 years in ambulatory care, working in women's health nutrition, mindful eating and behaviour change.

people.name: Jess White
people.credentials: Therapist and Sleep Support, MA, RP
bio: Registered Psychotherapist and sleep specialist with advanced CBT-i training, working on sleep disruption across reproductive life stages.

people.name: Amanda Thebe
bio: Fitness and menopause educator, speaker, and author specializing in perimenopause strength training and lifestyle wellness.

people.name: Sharon Lorber
bio: Registered Social Worker with more than 20 years supporting clients across reproductive life stages, from adolescence through menopause.

people.name: Sonia Taylor
people.credentials: NP, RN (EC), Psychotherapist, MSc, BScN, NCMP
bio: Nurse Practitioner and certified menopause practitioner with over 20 years in women's health, ADHD and mental health care.

people.name: Dr. Maryna Mammoliti
bio: Dr. Maryna Mammoliti is a Canadian psychiatrist, educator, physician leadership expert, and internationally recognized speaker with a special interest in ADHD, physician wellness, workplace functioning, and neurodiversity.

She has focused her psychiatric practice on ADHD, PTSD, eating disorders, and physician health and wellness for the past 11 years. She has authored peer-reviewed publications and presented on ADHD across the lifespan, ADHD in physicians, and ADHD and workplace functioning.
She runs DBT skill-based groups for moms with ADHD in Ontario and Alberta and advocates for strength-based, multidisciplinary approaches to ADHD across the lifespan.

people.name: Dr. Leslie Buckley
bio: Dr. Leslie Buckley is an Addiction Psychiatrist and Chief of the Addictions Division at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH) in Toronto. Leslie completed an Addiction Psychiatry fellowship at Yale University and specializes in providing outpatient treatment for substance use disorders and concurrent disorders.

She also holds a Masters in Public Health from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Areas of interest include understanding pathways to substance use disorders as well as gender differences and the implementation of more accessible and earlier interventions in substance use health.
Dr. Buckley is an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto, with longstanding involvement in addiction education for medical students and residents.

people.name: Dr. Lauren Uslinov
bio: Psychiatrist with extensive experience treating women across the reproductive lifespan in hospital and private clinic settings, with training in DBT, CBT, and Psychodynamic Psychotherapy.

people.name: Tara MacLeod
bio: Primary Care and Mental Health Nurse Practitioner with over 15 years of experience focusing on ADHD care, women's health, menopause support, and integrated mental health care.
